name: Glucagon

card.summary: A pancreatic hormone that raises blood sugar and influences fat metabolism; its receptor is part of newer dual-agonist weight-loss drugs aimed at reducing body fat.
card.note: Glucagon itself is an emergency hypoglycemia drug; weight-loss research involves GLP-1 and dual agonists.

quick.overview:
Glucagon is a 29-amino-acid peptide hormone made by pancreatic alpha cells. It works opposite to insulin, signalling the liver to release glucose during fasting, exercise or low blood sugar, and it also affects fat metabolism and energy balance.

For appearance, the link is body fat. Glucagon itself is mainly an emergency medicine, but drugs that combine GLP-1 and glucagon receptor activity are being tested for weight and liver-fat reduction, and forum users discuss insulin and glucagon as the drivers of fat gain and loss.
quick.how: Medical glucagon is a rescue injection for severe low blood sugar, given by caregivers or clinicians. In physique communities it is mostly discussed conceptually, through eating patterns that affect insulin and glucagon, or through GLP-1 and dual-agonist drugs. This page does not cover use or sourcing of any drug.
quick.risks: Glucagon rescue products can cause nausea and vomiting. Related GLP-1 receptor agonists are associated with gastrointestinal effects and with gallbladder events in meta-analyses, and some lean mass is lost along with fat during weight loss.

lead: Glucagon is a peptide hormone from the alpha cells of the pancreatic islets that raises blood glucose by stimulating the liver to break down glycogen and make new glucose. It is the main counter-regulatory hormone to insulin, and it also promotes the breakdown of stored fat. It was identified in 1922 as a blood-sugar-raising factor in pancreatic extracts.[1][12]

Its relevance to appearance runs through body composition. In physique and looksmaxxing forums, insulin and glucagon are discussed as the hormones that govern fat storage and fat burning, and users link meal composition, protein, carbohydrate and fasting to them.[2][21][22] In medicine, the glucagon receptor has become a drug target: dual agonists that activate both the GLP-1 and glucagon receptors (survodutide, mazdutide, pemvidutide) and the triple agonist retatrutide (GLP-1, GIP and glucagon) are studied for weight and liver-fat reduction.[3][4][14][15][16]

Clinically, synthetic glucagon is sold as an emergency rescue medicine for severe hypoglycemia and is not a cosmetic product.[13] This article covers the hormone, its role in fat metabolism, the drugs built around its receptor, and how the topic is discussed online.

paras: Glucagon is a linear 29-amino-acid peptide made from the precursor proglucagon in pancreatic alpha cells by the enzyme prohormone convertase 2. The same precursor yields GLP-1 and GLP-2 in the L cells of the intestine, which is why the three hormones share a family and why drugs can be designed to hit more than one of their receptors.[1][12] Oxyntomodulin, a 37-amino-acid gut peptide from the same family, binds both the GLP-1 and glucagon receptors and has been described as appetite-suppressing.[17]

The pancreas releases glucagon when blood glucose falls. Low blood sugar, adrenaline and amino acids such as arginine and alanine stimulate secretion, while insulin, somatostatin, amylin and GLP-1 suppress it.[12] Protein-rich meals also raise glucagon alongside insulin, a point that comes up repeatedly in physique forums.[1][21]

Glucagon binds a G-protein-coupled receptor on liver cells, raises intracellular cyclic AMP and activates protein kinase A, which switches liver metabolism toward glycogen breakdown and glucose production.[12] A 2024 review in Physiological Reviews describes hepatic glucagon action as reaching beyond glucose mobilization, into amino acid and lipid handling.[5]

sections.h: Role in fat and energy metabolism
paras: Wikipedia describes glucagon as the body's main catabolic hormone: it raises blood fatty acids as well as glucose, promotes lipolysis and reduces fatty-acid synthesis in the liver and fat tissue.[12] That catabolic profile, the mirror image of insulin's storage role, is the reason the hormone appears in discussions of fat loss and body recomposition.

Researchers developing obesity drugs add glucagon-receptor activity to GLP-1 activity because the two have complementary effects. GLP-1 reduces appetite and slows gastric emptying, while glucagon signalling is proposed to raise energy expenditure and clear liver fat. A dual agonist therefore aims to lower body weight through reduced intake and through added fat metabolism, and to reduce liver fat directly.[3][4][15] Early human data with oxyntomodulin, which activates both receptors, showed more weight lost over four weeks than saline in overweight volunteers.[17]

Synthetic glucagon is an emergency treatment for severe hypoglycemia when a person cannot take sugar by mouth. Its other labelled and clinical uses include relaxing the duodenum during endoscopic imaging, easing food impaction in the esophagus, and treating beta-blocker overdose.[13] The US approved glucagon in 1960 and it is on the WHO Essential Medicines List.[13]

Because glucagon is unstable in solution, older rescue kits required powder to be mixed with a diluent before injection. A nasal powder product (Baqsimi) was approved in the US and Canada in 2019, a US generic followed in December 2020, and the EU approved Ogluo for severe hypoglycemia in diabetes in February 2021.[13]

Glucagon itself is not used for cosmetic purposes. Its connection to looks is that drugs engaging its receptor are being developed to reduce body fat, and that people trying to change their physique discuss the insulin-glucagon balance in relation to diet.[2][4][21] Weight loss from these drugs can change facial and body appearance, including leaner contours, and clinicians also track lean-mass changes alongside fat loss.[3]

Several drug candidates combine glucagon-receptor activity with GLP-1 activity. Mazdutide (IBI362, LY3305677), an oxyntomodulin analogue developed by Innovent and Eli Lilly, was studied in phase 1b trials published in 2021 and 2022, including a randomized trial in Chinese patients with type 2 diabetes.[10][16] According to Wikipedia, a phase 3 report in the New England Journal of Medicine in May 2025 described clinically relevant weight reductions in Chinese adults with overweight or obesity, and the injection was approved for marketing in China in June 2025.[16]

Survodutide (BI 456906), developed by Boehringer Ingelheim, is a glucagon analogue acting as a GLP-1 and glucagon dual agonist. A 2025 analysis of three randomized trials (1,088 patients) found average body-weight reductions of roughly 7 to 9 percent after 4 to 11 months, and a phase 3 trial in adults with obesity and liver disease reported superiority to placebo for liver fat and body weight; gastrointestinal effects were the most common adverse events.[15] Pemvidutide, another GLP-1/glucagon dual agonist, was tested in a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study of people with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), with liver fat content as the main measure.[4]

Retatrutide, an Eli Lilly peptide that activates GLP-1, GIP and glucagon receptors, is described by Wikipedia as an experimental triple agonist. Its phase 2 results were published in the New England Journal of Medicine in August 2023, and the TRIUMPH phase 3 program reported mean weight reductions of 17.6, 23.7 and 25.0 percent at three weekly dose levels over 80 weeks, against 3.9 percent with placebo, in adults with obesity and no diabetes.[14] Meta-analyses summarised on the page report weight loss of about 15 to 24 percent over 48 to 72 weeks.[14]

A 2025 network meta-analysis of 22 trials found that GLP-1 receptor agonists reduced body weight by about 3.6 kg, fat mass by about 3 kg and lean mass by about 0.9 kg, with lean mass making up roughly a quarter of the weight lost while relative lean mass was unchanged.[3] A meta-analysis of 47 randomized trials examined weight, BMI and waist circumference in people with obesity or overweight.[6]

A trial of liraglutide in people with obesity and prediabetes examined insulin sensitivity separately from weight loss,[25] and a randomized trial of semaglutide in nonalcoholic steatohepatitis examined liver outcomes.[11] A trial pairing an SGLT2 inhibitor with a glucagon receptor antagonist in type 1 diabetes looked at the opposite direction, blocking glucagon action.[26]

Glucagon rescue products commonly cause vomiting, nausea and headache, and can lower potassium or blood pressure; they can increase bleeding risk in people on oral anticoagulants. They are contraindicated in pheochromocytoma and insulinoma, and use in pregnancy has not been found to harm the baby.[13]

For GLP-1 receptor agonists, meta-analyses report gastrointestinal adverse events and examine links to gallbladder and biliary disease.[7][8] A 2025 JAMA Psychiatry meta-analysis examined psychiatric and quality-of-life outcomes.[9] For retatrutide, Wikipedia lists nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, constipation and abdominal discomfort as the most common effects, more frequent at higher doses, with long-term outcomes still being studied.[14] Excess glucagon is itself clinically significant: a pancreatic glucagonoma produces too much of it, and unchecked glucagon release contributes to ketoacidosis in poorly controlled type 1 diabetes.[12]

Glucagon rescue products are prescription medicines in the US and elsewhere.[13] The dual and triple agonists are investigational drugs in most countries, with mazdutide approved in China as of 2025.[16] Wikipedia reports that unlicensed sellers marketed retatrutide as a research peptide before any approval, that Eli Lilly filed suits against six companies in August 2026, and that the Guardian covered consumers buying it through the grey market.[14] This wiki does not cover use or sourcing of these compounds.

A looksmax.org post titled around not counting calories argued that calories are a corporate-conditioned idea and that people who cannot lose weight should be tracking insulin and glucagon; one reply held that eating below one's needs causes loss and above causes gain, and another pointed to the bodybuilder Sam Sulek as a guide.[2]

On T Nation, glucagon appears in explanations of why protein does not spike blood sugar the way carbohydrate does: posters write that protein raises insulin and glucagon together, so blood sugar stays steadier.[21][22] Others describe a time course over a long fast in which insulin falls, fat burning rises and glucagon increases.[1] Threads about GLP-1 drugs mention that semaglutide suppresses glucagon secretion in a glucose-dependent way and improves insulin sensitivity.[23] Fat-loss drug discussion in physique communities increasingly mentions the dual and triple agonists by name.

Trials of GLP-1 and dual agonists cover body composition,[3] weight loss,[6] liver fat,[4][15] insulin sensitivity independent of weight loss with liraglutide,[25] and cardiovascular and kidney outcomes of long-acting and oral GLP-1 agonists in type 2 diabetes.[24] Phase 1b data exist for the dual agonist IBI362 in Chinese patients with type 2 diabetes.[10] One trial combined an SGLT2 inhibitor with a glucagon receptor antagonist in type 1 diabetes.[26] No studies found of glucagon itself as a cosmetic or physique treatment.

timeline.event: Glucagon identified as a hyperglycemic factor in pancreatic extracts and named by Kimball and Murlin.[1][12]
Eli Lilly scientists isolate and crystallize glucagon; its amino acid sequence is worked out in the late 1950s.[12][13]
Roger Unger's group develops the first radioimmunoassay for glucagon.[12]
Glucagon approved for medical use in the United States.[13]
Lund and Goodman show the proglucagon gene also encodes GLP-1 and GLP-2.[12]
Nasal glucagon (Baqsimi) approved in the US and Canada.[13]
Ogluo approved in the EU; phase 1b mazdutide results begin to appear.[13][16]
Phase 2 retatrutide results published in the New England Journal of Medicine (August).[14]
Mazdutide approved for marketing in China (June); survodutide pooled analysis and pemvidutide liver-fat trial published.[4][15][16]
Phase 3 TRIUMPH retatrutide results published; Lilly files suits against grey-market sellers (August).[14]

lore.intro: On looksmax.org and T Nation, glucagon appears in threads about hormones, diet and fat-loss drugs.

claims.claim: Insulin and glucagon, not calories, decide weight
claims.believers: The original poster says people cannot lose weight because they believe in calories and are not tracking these two hormones.[2]
claims.experts: Reviews and trials of weight-loss drugs report outcomes in body weight and fat mass,[3] and a reply in the thread argued that eating below needs causes loss.[2]

claims.claim: Protein is safe for blood sugar because it raises glucagon alongside insulin
claims.believers: T Nation posters write that protein triggers an insulin response but also glucagon, which blunts the blood sugar rise compared with carbohydrate.[21][22]
claims.experts: Physiology texts describe amino acids such as arginine and alanine as glucagon stimulators, and insulin as a suppressor of its release.[12]

claims.claim: Long fasts shift the body toward glucagon-driven fat burning
claims.believers: One T Nation poster lays out a fasting timeline in which insulin drops, fat burning rises and glucagon increases.[1]
claims.experts: Glucagon is described as the main catabolic, counter-regulatory hormone that raises fatty acids and promotes lipolysis.[12]

claims.claim: Adding glucagon action to GLP-1 drugs improves fat loss
claims.believers: Interest in dual and triple agonists reflects the view that a third receptor adds fat burning beyond appetite control.
claims.experts: Trials of survodutide, pemvidutide and retatrutide report weight and liver-fat reductions, with gastrointestinal effects the most common adverse events.[4][14][15]

claims.claim: GLP-1 drugs cost muscle as well as fat
claims.believers: Physique forum users often worry that weight loss from these drugs removes lean tissue.
claims.experts: A 2025 network meta-analysis found lean mass made up roughly a quarter of weight lost, with relative lean mass unchanged.[3]

claims.believers: Forum discussion treats insulin and glucagon as levers for fat gain and loss.[2]
claims.experts: Clinically, glucagon is a rescue drug for severe hypoglycemia, and no studies of it as a physique treatment have been found.[13]
